$comment: v2.3 plan 11 §Fault matrix. Eleven stateful packages against ten fault shapes (v2.4 plan 03 added the `aborted` shape and the `hostDeletes` package, decision E8; v2.4 plan 05 added `wiEvidence`, v2.5 plan 01 `wiNormalize`), one row per cell, each either citing the test that demonstrates it or saying what is not yet demonstrated. Generated set, hand-classified status. The guard in src/runtime/faultMatrix.guard.test.ts fails when this file and the code disagree: a missing pair, a row for a pair the matrix does not have, a citation whose test is not in the file it names, or an unproven cell that still cites something. Statuses: covered (a test asserts the designed behaviour for this package under this fault) | partial (a test covers part of it, and the note says which part) | todo (nothing covers it) | na (the shape cannot apply, and the note says why).

extraction|backendUnavailable.note: v2.4 plan 03 D3: a dead backend opens an in-memory breaker keyed by profile (never persisted): reads are held, extraction.enabled is never written, and a probe (5 s/15 s/60 s/300 s, online-status, profile update, Try again) resumes the held queue. A missing or deleted profile is config (not-configured + Repair), not transport. Previously partial: The surface names an enabled-but-unprofiled extraction; no test drives the scheduler itself with no reachable profile. v2.4 acceptance A6 (2026-09-25): a SLOW backend is not a dead one. J7 held reads ~32 min on a queued pod because every probe had a fixed 10 s budget; the probe budget now follows the backoff step (10 s/15 s/60 s/300 s cap), floored by the slowest call the profile answered recently, and any real call that answers on the profile closes its breaker. A refusing host keeps the same probe schedule, and a host that never answers gets one bounded probe at a time.

scene|beforeHostWrite.note: AE04-S1 closed 2026-09-25. The tracker's host write is refused ({ok:false}, the answer setStoryExtensionPrompt gives when the build has no setExtensionPrompt): sync() records `injected` only on ok, so the next sync writes the same block again and it lands; a permanent refusal is retried on every sync and journaled once with the host's reason; the stored read survives. Control: a write that lands is made once. Before the fix `injected` was set before the write and the WriteResult was discarded by the dep's `=> void` type, so a refusal stuck forever.

scene|afterHostWrite.note: v2.4 acceptance A1 (2026-09-25). The fault after the write is the host losing it: ST's clearChat reassigns `extension_prompts = {}` on every chat load, a same-chat reloadCurrentChat included (script.js:1590, 1712). The tracker used to compare against its own `injected` memo (and the seam against its `lastWritten` memo), so a block ST had dropped was never written again. sync() now compares against the block the host holds (`applied`, wired to readInjectedPromptBlocks in runtime/index.ts) and the seam reads getContext().extensionPrompts. Control: while the host still holds the block, nothing is rewritten. Replaces the na row, which said no post-write fault could be injected.

stagecraft|duplicateCompletion.note: AE-01 review (2026-09-25): the old citation ran ONE pass and checked `dueForRun()`, which delivers no duplicate. This test completes one accepted op twice: a second `applyAccepted` for the same boundary starts while the first is held at its host write. Both used to read the op as accepted and write it (2 host writes); applies are now serialized, so it is one host write, one `applied` op in one record and one journal line. Its control ("control: an op accepted while the first apply is at the host is written by the second") proves the second apply is not simply dropped: an op accepted mid-apply is still written, and the first apply's patch no longer erases a record appended during its awaits. The sequential repeat is pinned too ("the same boundary applied again after it finished is a no-op"). The curator pass itself cannot complete twice for one call; a second pass while one is in flight is refused by the hold ("coalesces: one pass per boundary gap, and never while one is in flight").

effects|delayedSuccess.evidence: src/runtime/effectsOwnership.review.test.ts#a checkpoint applied in its own chat stages everything and marks itself applied

effects|delayedError.evidence: src/runtime/effectLedger.test.ts#is left alone when the host cannot be read at all

NOT COVERED: no test makes a host write REJECT (throw) after a wait.

effects|malformedResponse.note: Effects consume no model response; the only answer they read is the host's own write result, which the host-write cells cover.

effects|duplicateCompletion.evidence: src/runtime/effectsApplier.test.ts#fires a one-shot reply once when the same checkpoint is applied twice, and twice when it is asked to
effects|duplicateCompletion.note: The same checkpoint applied twice fires the one-shot reply once; the counter key names the checkpoint, trigger, member and reply index.

effects|backendUnavailable.evidence: src/services/stHost/capabilities.test.ts#names the commands an effects path needs and this build does not have
effects|backendUnavailable.note: The effects path's backend is the host command surface: a missing one is probed and named, not discovered at use.

effects|beforeHostWrite.evidence: src/runtime/effectLedger.test.ts#never landed when the host still holds the old value
effects|beforeHostWrite.note: A recorded write that never landed is reconciled as dropped.

effects|afterHostWrite.evidence: src/runtime/effectLedger.test.ts#was applied when the host holds the new value
effects|afterHostWrite.note: The write landed with no answer recorded; the reconciler confirms it applied.

effects|persistFailure.evidence: src/runtime/effectsApplier.test.ts#refuses it, and says why, when the pending row is still unsaved
effects|persistFailure.note: FOUND BY THIS CENSUS and FIXED: the applier persisted the write-ahead pending row and then ran the host write regardless, and persist() cannot say whether the row reached disk (saveMetadata swallows its own errors). It now reads the save-evidence seam (`unsaved`, i.e. hasUnsavedChanges) after the write-ahead persist and REFUSES the effect, marking the row failed with PENDING_NOT_SAVED — no effect without a durable record. The sibling case (the row is saved, the effect runs) is the same describe block.

effects|worldSwitched.evidence: src/runtime/effectsOwnership.review.test.ts#a chat switch stops the sequence before the cast change reaches the shared group
effects|worldSwitched.note: The sequence stops before the write that outlives the chat.

effects|aborted.evidence: src/runtime/npcRepliesOwnership.review.test.ts#a chat switch during a generating reply writes nothing into the departed chat's state
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/npcRepliesOwnership.review.test.ts#a generating reply in a chat that did not move records its own last message
effects|aborted.note: Was na ("performs no model call"), which was wrong: an `llm` NPC reply is `/trigger await=true`, a main-model generation (v2.5 plan 02 C1). COVERED (v2.4 follow-up 2026-09-25): a sequence whose chat moved during the awaited reply writes nothing after it (the post-await check in fireNpcReplies); control: an unmoved chat records its own last message. NOT COVERED: nothing cancels the in-flight generation (executeSlashCommands takes no signal, nothing calls stopGeneration), and where that reply lands after a switch is unmeasured; the stop is v2.5 plan 02 C1 step 2, measure-first.

hostDeletes|delayedSuccess.evidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#deletes a marked book whose chat is confirmed gone, after the player says yes
hostDeletes|delayedSuccess.note: v2.4 plan 02 T14 (E8): the reap waits on the presence probe and the player's confirm, and deletes only the marked book of the chat the marker names once both answer.

hostDeletes|delayedError.evidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#keeps serving events after one reap throws
hostDeletes|delayedError.note: A reap that throws late does not take the listener down; the next deletion is still handled.

hostDeletes|malformedResponse.evidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#refuses another owner, a missing chat id and non-JSON
hostDeletes|malformedResponse.note: A so-owner marker that is not ours, names no chat or is not JSON never makes a book reapable.

hostDeletes|duplicateCompletion.evidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#asks one question at a time when a group delete announces several chats
hostDeletes|duplicateCompletion.note: COVERED: several deletions announced together are serialised, one question at a time. NOT COVERED: no test delivers the same deletion event twice.

hostDeletes|backendUnavailable.evidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#turns a deletion it cannot confirm into a Repair row, never a delete
hostDeletes|backendUnavailable.note: A presence probe that cannot answer is never read as 'the chat is gone': the book stays and a Repair row names it.

hostDeletes|beforeHostWrite.evidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#leaves no row and attempts no delete when the book was deleted elsewhere while the confirm was open
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#requires the player's yes: a declined reap keeps the book and leaves a Repair row
hostDeletes|beforeHostWrite.note: Everything that can change before the delete (the book removed elsewhere, the player declining) is re-read and stops the delete.

hostDeletes|afterHostWrite.evidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#reports a refused delete as a Repair row with the host's reason
hostDeletes|afterHostWrite.note: A delete the host refuses is not counted as done: the book keeps a Repair row carrying the host's reason.

hostDeletes|persistFailure.note: The reaper persists nothing: its Repair rows are in-memory and re-derived, and the chat it serves is already deleted.

hostDeletes|worldSwitched.evidence: src/runtime/mirrorReaper.review.test.ts#deletes nothing once the runtime stopped while the confirm was open
hostDeletes|worldSwitched.note: The reaper's world is the runtime's lifetime, not a chat (the chat is gone by construction); a runtime that stopped while the confirm was open deletes nothing and leaves a lapsed row.

hostDeletes|aborted.note: Performs no model call, so nothing can be cancelled mid-call.

wiEvidence|delayedSuccess.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoEvidence.test.ts#tags several scans of one generation instead of merging them, and a quiet scan never counts as the reply
wiEvidence|delayedSuccess.note: v2.4 plan 05 T12: a scan that arrives later in the same loud generation lands in that generation's slot, tagged by the run it fired in.

wiEvidence|delayedError.note: Read-only observers of host events: nothing is awaited, so nothing can fail late.

wiEvidence|malformedResponse.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoEvidence.test.ts#drops an activated entry that names no book or no uid instead of recording a guess
wiEvidence|malformedResponse.note: An activated entry without a world or a finite uid is dropped, never recorded as a guess.

wiEvidence|duplicateCompletion.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoEvidence.test.ts#the same entry activated by two scans of one generation is one fired row
wiEvidence|duplicateCompletion.note: Recursion or a second scan reporting the same entry does not double it.

wiEvidence|backendUnavailable.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoEvidence.test.ts#with no loud scan observed there is nothing to judge, so a slot raises no flag
wiEvidence|backendUnavailable.note: A generation that never reached a scan (an interceptor abort, a backend that failed first) raises no miss flag: ST emits nothing for 'no scan' and nothing for 'nothing fired' (05-H1).

wiEvidence|persistFailure.note: The ring is memory-only; its miss flags persist only as journal records through the ordinary chat save, which the persistence package covers.

wiEvidence|worldSwitched.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoEvidence.test.ts#a new world drops every slot, and another chat's slots are never shown
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/worldInfoEvidence.test.ts#an edit at or before a slot's reply drops it; one after it keeps it (inv 11)
wiEvidence|worldSwitched.note: A story load, restart or chat change drops every slot; an edit at or before a slot's reply drops that slot.

wiEvidence|aborted.note: Performs no model call, so nothing can be cancelled mid-call.

wiNormalize|delayedSuccess.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoGating.test.ts#confirmed: normalises first, then activates (W2); a scan before that runs the file path
wiNormalize|delayedSuccess.note: v2.5 plan 01: a lorebook write held open and released later lands, is recorded, and only then does the scan view activate; until then scans run the file path.

wiNormalize|delayedError.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoGating.test.ts#a write that throws late records nothing, never activates, journals why, and the next sync still runs
wiNormalize|delayedError.note: A host write that rejects after the wait records nothing in the ledger, leaves the file path in charge, journals the reason, and does not take the gating down: the next settings write retries it.

wiNormalize|malformedResponse.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoNormalize.test.ts#never records an entry the book does not hold, or a book that is not listed
wiNormalize|malformedResponse.note: A book read that is not listed, or that lacks a gated comment, is never recorded as normalised; the entry is picked up once it exists.

wiNormalize|duplicateCompletion.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoNormalize.test.ts#flips exactly the gated entries of every listed library book, once: the second run writes nothing
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/worldInfoNormalize.test.ts#a gated set that grows normalises only what is new
wiNormalize|duplicateCompletion.note: A second normalisation over the same library writes nothing (the ledger is incremental), and a grown set writes only the new entries.

wiNormalize|backendUnavailable.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoGating.test.ts#an absent capability keeps the file path, says why, and writes nothing
wiNormalize|backendUnavailable.note: A host whose scans cannot be gated (the wiScanGating capability absent or erroring) keeps the file path, says why in the status, and normalises nothing; an unreadable book is skipped, never written blind.

wiNormalize|beforeHostWrite.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoNormalize.test.ts#stops before a write once its run has lapsed
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/worldInfoGating.test.ts#the confirm gates the first write: cancelling leaves file mode and writes nothing
wiNormalize|beforeHostWrite.note: The run is asked immediately before each book's write, and nothing is written before the author's confirm. A book deleted between the read and the write (the host-deletes shape) is refused by the typed write (`there is no lorebook`) and recorded as refused, never as normalised: see the afterHostWrite citation.

wiNormalize|afterHostWrite.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoNormalize.test.ts#a refused or unconfirmed write is not recorded as normalised, so the next run retries it
wiNormalize|afterHostWrite.note: A write the server refused, or whose read-back could not confirm it, never enters the ledger; the next run re-reads the file and retries (W4: an entry that did land is then recorded through the already-off branch).

wiNormalize|persistFailure.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoNormalize.test.ts#records what each entry was before it was normalised, and writes nothing for an entry already resting off
wiNormalize|persistFailure.note: COVERED: an entry that rests off in its file but is missing from the ledger (a ledger save that never landed, W4) is recorded on the next run without a write, as wasOn false. NOT COVERED: its provenance is then lost (the original wasOn true is not recoverable), so a later removal restore cannot offer it; stated as the W4 risk, not hidden.

wiNormalize|worldSwitched.evidence: src/runtime/worldInfoGating.test.ts#stopping the gating mid-normalisation stops before the next write, records nothing and never activates
alsoEvidence: src/runtime/worldInfoGating.test.ts#control: an unstopped run normalises both books
wiNormalize|worldSwitched.note: The normaliser's world is the gating's lifetime, not a chat (its writes are install-wide lorebook state): stopping the runtime mid-run stops before the next book and never activates; a chat switch deliberately does not stop it, because half a gated set would leak.

wiNormalize|aborted.note: Performs no model call, so nothing can be cancelled mid-call.
